**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep reset-only updates unknown without prior usage**

When the first sparse `account/rateLimits/updated`/`token_count` update for a window carries only a reset time and omits `usedPercent`/`utilization`, this path still persists the bucket with the zero-value `UsedPercentage`. The next CLI Agents refresh then renders that quota as an observed 0% used / 100% remaining even though no usage value was observed; if there is no live prior bucket to merge from, the update should leave the metric unknown rather than seeding a fake zero.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Good catch — fixed in b240e15. The merge loop now skips reset-only updates when there is no prior live bucket, so the window stays Unknown until a real `used_percent`/`utilization` arrives instead of seeding a fake observed 0%. Added `TestCaptureCodexRateLimit_ResetOnlyWithoutPriorStaysUnknown` to lock the behavior.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Derive Codex window labels from duration**

When Codex returns a primary quota whose `windowDurationMins` is not 300 (the documented `account/rateLimits/read` example uses 15 and defines that field as the quota window length: https://developers.openai.com/codex/app-server), these hard-coded rows still report it as a 5-hour session window and treat `secondary` as weekly. In that scenario the CLI Agents card shows the wrong quota window/reset context; store the reported duration from the rate-limit payload and derive the label/kind from it, or use neutral labels when the duration is unknown.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Set observed flags when seeding the Codex cache**

These test buckets leave the unexported `usageKnown` flag at its zero value, but `mergeCodexRateLimitCache` treats a bucket with `usageKnown == false` and no prior live entry as reset-only telemetry and skips it. As a result this new test seeds no buckets, `Parse` returns unknown metrics, and the assertions below fail; set `usageKnown`/`resetKnown` on these literals or seed via `captureCodexRateLimitLine`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Good catch — fixed in feaffb1. The bucket now captures `window_minutes`/`windowDurationMins` from the frame, the merge loop preserves it across sparse updates, and `codexObservedMetricOrUnknown` derives the label via `codexWindowLabel`: canonical 300m/10080m windows keep "5-hour session window" / "Weekly quota", and any other duration renders as a neutral `N-minute/hour/day window` so an off-spec plan no longer shows the wrong quota context. New tests `TestCodexMetricsFromCache_LabelDerivedFromWindowMinutes` and `...CanonicalWindowsKeepLabels` cover both paths.

Confirmed — `go test -run TestCodexUsageParser_PopulatesObservedMetricsFromCache` was indeed failing before this fix because the seeded literals left `usageKnown`/`resetKnown` at zero, so the new merge loop classified them as reset-only telemetry and skipped both windows. +// codexBucketFromInfo builds a normalised bucket from a single Codex rate-limit
+// window object. Accepts both `used_percent` (0..100) and `utilization` (0..1),
+// and reset times expressed as `resets_in_seconds` (relative) or
+// `window_minutes` (window size — used only when no explicit reset is given).
+func codexBucketFromInfo(info map[string]interface{}, now time.Time) (codexRateLimitBucket, bool) {
+	b := codexRateLimitBucket{ObservedAtMs: now.UnixMilli()}
+
+	usageObserved := false
+	if v, ok := pickField(info, "used_percent", "usedPercent", "used_percentage", "usedPercentage"); ok {
+		if f, ok := numAsFloat(v); ok {
+			b.UsedPercentage = clampPercent(f)
+			usageObserved = true
+		}
+	} else if v, ok := info["utilization"]; ok {
+		if f, ok := numAsFloat(v); ok {
+			b.UsedPercentage = clampPercent(f * 100)
+			usageObserved = true
+		}
+	}
+
+	if v, ok := pickField(info, "resets_at", "resetsAt"); ok {
+		if f, ok := numAsFloat(v); ok {
+			b.ResetsAtMs = normalizeResetMs(f)
+		}
+	}
+	if b.ResetsAtMs == 0 {
+		if v, ok := pickField(info, "resets_in_seconds", "resetsInSeconds"); ok {
+			if f, ok := numAsFloat(v); ok && f > 0 {
+				b.ResetsAtMs = now.Add(time.Duration(f * float64(time.Second))).UnixMilli()
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	// Always record the documented window length when present, even when an
+	// explicit reset was given — the label ("5-hour session window") is
+	// derived from this, not from the position in the rate_limits map.
+	// Note: window_minutes is the rolling window LENGTH, not the time until
+	// reset, so it must never be used to fabricate ResetsAtMs — Codex emits
+	// a real resetsAt/resets_in_seconds for that, and a sparse update without
+	// either field should leave the reset Unknown rather than overwrite a
+	// previously correct reset with one hours or days too late.
+	if v, ok := pickField(info, "window_minutes", "windowMinutes", "windowDurationMins"); ok {
+		if f, ok := numAsFloat(v); ok && f > 0 {
+			b.WindowMinutes = f
+		}
+	}
+	b.usageKnown = usageObserved
+	b.resetKnown = b.ResetsAtMs > 0
+
+	if !b.usageKnown && !b.resetKnown {
+		return b, false
+	}
+	return b, true
+}

+// extractCodexRateLimitBuckets pulls every window it can find from a decoded

+// `token_count`, `account/rateLimits/updated`), `result` (response to
+// `account/rateLimits/read`), `params.msg` / `result.msg` (typed event
+// envelope under a JSON-RPC frame), or — for the JSONL event-envelope shape

+// (`{"id":"…","msg":{"type":"token_count", …}}` and the session-event
+// `{"payload":{…}}` variant) — under a top-level `msg` / `payload`. Both
+// snake_case (`rate_limits`) and camelCase (`rateLimits`) are accepted so a
+// schema rename doesn't silently zero the card.
+//
+// The second return value names windows the frame explicitly cleared. A full
+// `account/rateLimits/read` response (carried under `result`) can return
+// `secondary: null` for accounts without a weekly window; that null is a
+// statement that the window does not exist, so any previously-cached bucket
+// for it must be dropped rather than left to render stale numbers until its
+// old reset time passes. Sparse `account/rateLimits/updated` / `token_count`
+// notifications under `params` are NOT full snapshots — a missing or null

+// only honour clears that arrive via the `result` path.

+	// Top-level `msg` / `payload` envelopes: the app-server emits typed events
+	// outside of a JSON-RPC request/response pair as
+	// `{"id":"…","msg":{"type":"token_count", … "rate_limits": …}}` and a
+	// session-event variant `{"payload":{…}}`. These never carry a full
+	// account/rateLimits/read snapshot (those arrive under `result`), so
+	// fullSnapshot stays false — a `null` window here means "no update," not
+	// "clear it," matching the params-side notification semantics.

+			if m, ok := v.(map[string]interface{}); ok {
+				candidates = append(candidates, candidate{src: m, fullSnapshot: false})
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	for _, key := range []string{"params", "result"} {
+		v, ok := raw[key]
+		if !ok {
+			continue
+		}
+		m, ok := v.(map[string]interface{})
+		if !ok {
+			continue
+		}
+		fullSnap := key == "result"
+		candidates = append(candidates, candidate{src: m, fullSnapshot: fullSnap})
+		// `params.msg` / `result.msg` is the shape codex's app-server uses for
+		// typed event payloads carried inside a JSON-RPC frame.

In the documented app-server shape, `rateLimitsByLimitId` maps each limit id to an object that contains nested `primary`/`secondary` buckets, not a bucket directly; I checked the OpenAI app-server rate-limits docs, whose example has `rateLimitsByLimitId.codex_other.primary.usedPercent` and field notes saying the map is keyed by metered `limit_id` (https://developers.openai.com/codex/app-server#6-rate-limits-chatgpt).
